questions.question: Why do pure dense bi-encoder embeddings sometimes struggle with exact error codes or service names like 'PgBouncer'?

options.A: Bi-encoders compress whole sentences into one pooled vector, smoothing over rare exact tokens.

questions.explanation: Pooling entire sentences averages token representations; hybrid lexical/cross-encoder reranking restores exact token precision.
questions.implication: Technical logs depend heavily on exact identifiers (Exit 137, CVE IDs, RC=91); hybrid scoring prevents semantic drift.

questions.question: Why use a two-stage retrieve-then-rerank architecture instead of running a heavy reranker over all documents?

options.A: Stage 1 bi-encoder search scales fast over thousands of docs, while Stage 2 reranks only the Top-K candidates.

questions.explanation: Two-stage retrieval balances sub-10ms recall at scale with high-precision top-K ranking.
questions.implication: Running pairwise reranking across 100k documents would violate P1 SLA latency budgets; two-stage retrieval keeps latency bounded.

questions.question: What is the 'red herring' trap built into INCIDENTS[2] across all 6 domains?

options.A: A nominal CPU metric ('CPU at 22%..42%') paired with a specific subsystem bottleneck.

questions.explanation: It tests whether your retriever focuses on the true subsystem failure rather than generic CPU keywords.
questions.implication: Real monitoring alerts frequently include healthy baseline metrics alongside the actual anomaly.
